Here's the complete picture, pulled from `docs/security/` and the open tickets on the Trading & Fund board.

## The go-public gates (epic [#18](https://github.com/jdtogni78/dstrader-aws/issues/18))

Hard gates that must close **before** the flip:

| # | Status | What it does |
|---|--------|--------------|
| **#7**  | Open | Provision server age key on spirit; add as SOPS recipient; `sops updatekeys` |
| **#10** | Open | Owner-only: rotate burned TWS/IB + mail passwords, write `secrets/prod/*.sops` |
| **#11** | Open | Cut prod compose to `SECRETS_BACKEND=sops`, paper-validate on stage, retire GPG plumbing |
| **#12** | Open | Stand up least-privilege IB user (no transfers/withdrawals); auto-login points there |
| **#15** | Open | Re-clone prod host from `dstrader-docker` (fresh clone — no shared history with `dstrader-aws`) |
| **#8**  | **Closed** | Env-driven compose DB creds (landed in 7b0b2c7 / merge 1afb6b9) |

Then the flip itself:

| # | Status | What it does |
|---|--------|--------------|
| **#16** | Open | Human-only: `gh repo edit jdtogni78/dstrader-docker --visibility public …` |
| **#17** | Open | Post-flip: enable CodeQL default setup + SARIF upload |

Open architectural question — **[#19](https://github.com/jdtogni78/dstrader-aws/issues/19)** proposes superseding #16 with a brand-new repo `jdtogni78/dstrader-docker-public` seeded as a single squash commit of current HEAD (no rewritten history at all). If accepted it replaces #16 and re-targets #15. Worth a decision before doing the work in #15/#16.

## Cleanup items on #18 (no ticket — out-of-band)

- README/docs skim across tracked files for `/Users/(dtogni|claudio1|jdtogni)`, `jdtogni*@gmail.com`, `192.168.*`, `10.0.0.10`, `spirit`. I ran this — only 3 hits, all placeholder/doc-comment values:
  - `local/wakeonlan.py:8` — `192.168.1.255` example in usage string
  - `local/wake_spirit.sh:7` — `192.168.1.255` example in env-var comment, plus `spirit` only as the script's own filename
  - `docs/security/HISTORY-AUDIT.md` — intentional forensic refs (the doc said these can stay)
- Re-audit on the live `jdtogni78/dstrader-docker` origin: `gitleaks --all` + the §3 grep matrix → 0 findings.
- Archive `jdtogni78/dstrader-aws` after #15+#16 land (Phase 8 of the runbook).
- Re-clone any other dev hosts onto `dstrader-docker` + `dstrader-secrets`.

## Files documenting the plan

- `docs/security/HISTORY-AUDIT.md` — full-history audit, scrub recipe, dry-run validation table
- `docs/security/SWAP-PLAN.md` — clean-repo build + the original "push and swap" plan
- `docs/security/PROD-CUTOVER-RUNBOOK.md` — phased runbook (8 phases) mapping each ticket to its gate + verification step
- `docs/security/history-purge-paths.txt` — paths fed to `git filter-repo`

## Order of operations (per the runbook)

1. **Phase 1** — #7 server age key
2. **Phase 2** — #10 rotate + write `secrets/prod/*.sops`; #12 in parallel (same IB Account Management visit)
3. **Phase 3** — #11 stage paper E2E → prod cutover → GPG-retirement PR
4. **Phase 4** — #15 re-clone prod host
5. **Phase 5** — final audit on the live remote (mirror clone + gitleaks + grep matrix)
6. **Phase 6** — #16 the flip (human-only, irreversible)
7. **Phase 7** — #17 CodeQL/SARIF
8. **Phase 8** — archive `dstrader-aws`

The two human-only / irreversible steps are the IB password rotation (#10) and the visibility flip (#16). Everything else an agent can prep, but the runbook is explicit that agents must not run the rotation, the SOPS prod cutover, the prod-host re-clone, the visibility flip, any deploy, any force-push, or repo archival.

Do we have a, uh, replicate, uh, replicatable script to check for and sanitize the the kit history? Um, and, um, if we do, is there any part of it that uses AI? Can we make something that use part... use AI somehow?

## What exists today

**Check (fully automated, replicatable):**
- `.github/workflows/security-scan.yml` — gitleaks on PR/push/daily cron
- `.githooks/pre-commit` (staged content) + `.githooks/pre-push` (outgoing history) + shared `_gitleaks.sh` runner
- `bin/install-git-hooks.sh` — one-shot installer (`core.hooksPath -> .githooks`)
- `.gitleaks.toml` — config + allowlists
- Manual full-history audit recipe in `docs/security/HISTORY-AUDIT.md` §3 — `gitleaks detect --no-git` on a `--mirror` clone + a grep matrix (IB IDs, owner emails, internal IPs, `.pgp`, `Prescription.pdf`)

**Sanitize (documented recipe, human-gated, not a one-shot script):**
- `docs/security/history-purge-paths.txt` — feeds `git filter-repo --invert-paths --paths-from-file`
- Replace-text rules live **off-repo** at `~/dev/_repo-backups/2026-05-25-…/dstrader-aws-replace-rules.SECRET.txt` (they contain the actual secret values being redacted, so by design they don't ride in the repo)
- The force-push + downstream re-clone steps are the runbook in `HISTORY-AUDIT.md` §4 + `SWAP-PLAN.md` — deliberately not scripted because they're destructive and prod-touching

## Does any of it use AI?

No. Gitleaks is regex + entropy; the grep matrix is plain `git grep`; `filter-repo` is mechanical.

## Where AI could plausibly help

A few targeted spots, ordered roughly by signal-to-noise:

1. **Gitleaks false-positive triage** — pipe the JSON output (with values redacted, only surrounding context + file path + rule name) to an LLM and ask "real / test fixture / placeholder, and why." Could cut review time on the daily CI runs without ever sending the actual secret out.
2. **PII beyond regex** — the `Prescription.pdf` catch was a human eyeball moment; gitleaks ignored it because it's not a credential. An LLM scan over tracked-file names + a sample of contents could flag "this looks medical/legal/personal" or "this string looks like a real person's name in a config file."
3. **Replace-rule drafting** — feed it the audit findings, get a draft `--replace-text` mapping with the anchoring constraints from `HISTORY-AUDIT.md` baked into the prompt (e.g. "never bare 4-digit literals — anchor to `DB_PASSWORD=…`"). Still human-reviewed before running, but faster to draft.
4. **Hook UX** — when pre-commit blocks, an LLM could explain in plain English what triggered and propose the remediation (`.env` move, allowlist entry, history rewrite). Detection stays regex; the polish is AI.

**Where AI should not go:**
- Never send actual secret values to an external API — that just relocates the leak. Redact before the prompt.
- Don't let it drive the destructive step (`filter-repo`, force-push, prod re-clone). Those stay deterministic + human-gated.
- Don't replace gitleaks with an LLM classifier — you'd lose the reproducible/auditable property that lets you say "0 findings" with a straight face.

Want me to sketch a `bin/audit-history.sh` that wraps the §3 mirror-clone audit into one command, and a separate `bin/triage-gitleaks-json.sh` that pipes gitleaks output (values redacted) through Claude for FP triage? Those are the two pieces that would actually pay back — the rest of the runbook is irreversible enough that I'd leave it human-driven.

## The design

Three pieces, each independent. The deterministic scan stays the source of truth; AI contributes *rule discovery*, not *rule execution*.

### A. Full-history scan (deterministic, no AI)

A `bin/audit-history.sh` that codifies what `HISTORY-AUDIT.md` §3 does by hand:

```
1. git clone --mirror <origin> /tmp/audit.git
2. gitleaks detect --source /tmp/audit.git --no-git --redact --config .gitleaks.toml  # whole-history
3. grep matrix on a working-tree checkout:
     - regex patterns from .audit-rules.yaml (per-repo, committed)
     - file-name patterns (e.g. *.pgp, *.pdf outside docs/, *.key, *_private.*)
     - "binary in surprising place" — anything >1MB outside expected dirs
4. emit audit-report.json  +  audit-report.md
```

Replicatable: anyone can run it on any clone, output is diffable across runs.

### B. AI suggestion step (rule discovery)

A `bin/audit-suggest.sh` that asks Claude *what to look for*, never showing it the leaks themselves. Inputs sent to the model:

- File tree (paths only, no content)
- Language/framework markers (`composer.json`, `pom.xml` summary, Dockerfile FROM lines, key directories)
- README/CLAUDE.md
- A list of file *types* present (`.properties`, `.encr`, `.sops`, `.pdf`, …)
- The **schema** of `audit-report.json` from the deterministic run, with values redacted to `[REDACTED:entropy=4.2,len=18]`

Output: a Markdown report — "given this is a Java trading engine + Laravel app + Python GUI automation + MariaDB stack, here are 14 things worth checking that generic gitleaks rules will miss," each with a proposed regex, an example placeholder, and a why-this-applies-to-this-repo. **The operator reviews, picks the good ones, and commits them to `.audit-rules.yaml`** — so the AI's contribution becomes durable config, not a re-run-the-prompt-every-time dependency.

Hard rules in the prompt template:
- Never send real candidate secret values to the LLM.
- The LLM proposes rules; humans merge them; the deterministic scan runs them.

### C. Repo-archetype catalog (the watch-list you asked for)

This is the most reusable artifact — a doc the AI step *reads* to bootstrap suggestions, and that you can re-use on the next repo. Tailored to this stack:

| Archetype | What to grep / glob for | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Broker/trading creds** | `U[0-9]{7,8}`, `DU[0-9]{7,8}` (IB account IDs); `paperTradingAccount=`, `actualLiveAccount=` in `.properties`; refs to TWS ports `4002`/`7497` near a password | Already burned this repo once — see HISTORY-AUDIT.md §2 row 3 |
| **Java `.properties` files** | lines matching `(password\|passwd\|secret\|token\|apikey)\s*=\s*\S+` excluding `%PLACEHOLDER%`, `${VAR}` | DSTrader config style; `auto_login.properties` is the canonical case |
| **Laravel/PHP** | `APP_KEY=base64:`, `DB_PASSWORD=`, `MAIL_PASSWORD=`, committed `.env` (not `.env.example`), `database/seeders/*.php` with bcrypt hashes or real emails | FamilyFund side; `.env` discipline is the usual failure |
| **Docker Compose** | `MARIADB_*_PASSWORD: [^$]`, `DB_PASSWORD: [^$]` — i.e. literal not `${VAR}` | Closed in #8 but the regex is the regression guard |
| **GPG / SOPS** | `*.pgp` (entire file), `BEGIN .* PRIVATE KEY`, `~/.gnupg/` bind mounts in committed yaml, `*.gpg` adjacent to its ciphertext | This repo's original critical finding (#1) |
| **Database artifacts** | `datadir*/`, `*.ibd`, `*.frm`, `ibdata1`, `ib_logfile*`, `mysql-bin.*`, `*.sql` files >1MB | Finding #2 — 165 MB of raw user PII in history |
| **Image-based GUI automation** | every file under `auto_login/images/`, especially `*.pdf`, `*.png` >500KB, anything not also in `rects.json` | The `Prescription.pdf` catch — gitleaks doesn't see it |
| **Owner/operator PII** | `/Users/[a-z]+`, `[a-z.]+@gmail\.com`, hostnames matching a configured allow-list of "do not commit," MAC addresses, WoL targets | Personal-host names like `spirit`, dev-laptop paths, owner emails |
| **Internal network** | `192\.168\.\d+\.\d+`, `10\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+`, private DNS suffixes (`.lan`, `.local`, `.internal`) | Topology disclosure; OK in `.example` files only |
| **SSH / cloud** | `BEGIN .* PRIVATE KEY`, `ssh-rsa AAAA`, `AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}`, `aws_secret_access_key`, `*.pem`, `*.p12` in tracked files | Generic but cheap |
| **Backup / dump tarballs** | `*.tar.gz`, `*.zip`, `*.bak`, `*.dump` >1MB in tracked tree | The "I'll just keep a copy" footgun |
| **Cron / deploy scripts** | `mysqldump.*-p[^$]`, `mysql.*-p[^$]`, `curl.*-u\s+\S+:`, `sshpass`, `ANSIBLE_VAULT` | The script-embedded creds class (#8 finding row 3-5) |
| **Co-author / commit metadata** | committer emails matching a `personal-emails.txt` list, hostnames in trailers | Audit-noise filter, not a blocker |

The catalog lives at `docs/security/audit-archetypes.md`. The AI step reads it and says "this repo has 9 of these 13 archetypes; here are extra checks for the 9, and here are repo-specific patterns I'd add to .audit-rules.yaml."

## What's deliberately NOT here

- AI replacing gitleaks — keeps deterministic gate intact.
- AI seeing the actual matched values — redact before the prompt.
- AI driving the destructive `filter-repo` step — that stays a runbook.
